name: THE CLARION OFFICE

LOOK_AT.say: A paper spike, loaded to the hilt with stories that did not run.
repeat: The top sheet reads CORRECTION in capitals, and nothing else. It was spiked before he could think of one.
He spikes his own stories when better ones occur to him. The better ones are on the front page. The true ones are here.
then: It is the most accurate archive in the building.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing. A spike is where a story's life ends, and it is very quiet there.
repeat: Paper stirring when the door opens. The rejected, briefly hopeful.
Nothing. I will not be adding to it.

LOOK_AT.say: The only known likeness of Obadiah Mott. I have seen this exact photograph in Mr.
repeat: He has the look of a man who was asked to think of something noble and is thinking of lunch.
The photographer's stamp has been trimmed off the bottom, neatly. Somebody wanted this to be a picture of someone.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing. It is a picture of a man in Ohio.
repeat: Nothing. Whoever he is, he has not said a word in twelve years.
The frame ticks on its nail. It is the most this likeness has ever said.

LOOK_AT.say: A keg of printer's ink, black as a creditor's mood and nearly as hard to get off the hands.
repeat: There are black thumbprints on everything in this office, including, somehow, the ceiling.
The keg is stenciled ST. LOUIS. The news here is local; the black is imported.

LISTEN_TO.say: A thick, slow settle when the floor moves. It does not slosh. It considers.
repeat: Nothing. It is waiting to be turned into opinions.
The lid comes up with a reluctant kiss. I put it back down.

LOOK_AT.say: OBITUARY, PAGE ONE. 'THADEUS GRUBBE.' I have read my own death in the street, misspelled with great care.
LOOK_AT.sceneLine: docs/57-puzzle-completion.md::# THE RUNNING GAG, MADE VISIBLE — the Clarion's headlines · after E5

LOOK_AT.say: FUNERAL THURSDAY: THE PIANO MAN. They have not used my name at all. It is the most accurate they have been.
LOOK_AT.sceneLine: docs/57-puzzle-completion.md::# THE RUNNING GAG, MADE VISIBLE — the Clarion's headlines · after E3

LOOK_AT.say: MEMORIAL FOR E. PIKE, LATE. ALL WELCOME. REFRESHMENTS. Frame added the refreshments. He was right to.
LOOK_AT.sceneLine: docs/57-puzzle-completion.md::# THE RUNNING GAG, MADE VISIBLE — the Clarion's headlines · after C3

LOOK_AT.say: ASSAY QUEUE 'SLIMS,' SAYS LEDGER. 'Mr. GRUBBE, a client.' The E is back. It was always going to come back.
LOOK_AT.sceneLine: docs/57-puzzle-completion.md::# THE RUNNING GAG, MADE VISIBLE — the Clarion's headlines · after C5

LOOK_AT.say: VESSEL SIGNS! 'T. GRUB.' I won, and it cost me a letter.
LOOK_AT.sceneLine: docs/57-puzzle-completion.md::# THE RUNNING GAG, MADE VISIBLE — the Clarion's headlines · after B6

LOOK_AT.say: VESSEL TROUNCES NEWCOMER IN ASSAY. 'A Mr. Grubbe of the East.' I am now a region.
LOOK_AT.sceneLine: docs/57-puzzle-completion.md::# THE RUNNING GAG, MADE VISIBLE — the Clarion's headlines · after B5

LOOK_AT.say: DIVINER SURVEYS CLAIM TWO; EARTH 'BRIEF.' 'Mr. GRABB.' He has given me an A I did not ask for.
LOOK_AT.sceneLine: docs/57-puzzle-completion.md::# THE RUNNING GAG, MADE VISIBLE — the Clarion's headlines · after A7

LOOK_AT.say: RACCOON EVICTED BY PIANO MAN. 'Mr. GRUB.' I have lost a B to a raccoon.
LOOK_AT.sceneLine: docs/57-puzzle-completion.md::# THE RUNNING GAG, MADE VISIBLE — the Clarion's headlines · after A5

LOOK_AT.say: EASTERN GENTLEMAN BUYS CLAIM TWO, IS DELIGHTED. 'Mr. T. GRUBBS of Providence.' The S is new.
LOOK_AT.sceneLine: docs/57-puzzle-completion.md::# THE RUNNING GAG, MADE VISIBLE — the Clarion's headlines · after A3

LOOK_AT.say: The stage schedules, chalked: arrivals, departures, and a column headed DELAYED that has never once been empty.
repeat: One departure has been rubbed out with a thumb. Whoever left on it, Frame is keeping for himself.
The coach east runs Tuesdays. The coach west runs when it feels it has something to say.

LISTEN_TO.say: Chalk dust drifting off the ledge. Every departure leaves a little behind.
repeat: Nothing. A timetable is a silent form of optimism.
The board knocks against the wall when the press runs, in time with it. The whole building keeps the same bad rhythm.

overrides.CLOSE: Tomorrow's headline is chalked and facing the street. There is no closing the news. I have asked.

LOOK_AT.say: A desk under a drift of proofs, notes and half-sentences.
repeat: A card pinned to the top reads VERIFY. It has been there so long the ink has faded to a suggestion.
Every drawer is open. Nothing in this office has ever been kept back from print, including several things that should have been.
then: Somewhere beneath them, I am assured, is a desk.

LISTEN_TO.say: Paper, shifting whenever the press runs.
repeat: A pencil rolling slowly toward the edge. It has done this before, and nobody has stopped it.
Nothing, for once. The quietest place in the building is where he does his thinking, which may explain the paper.
then: The desk is in a permanent state of mild landslide.

LOOK_AT.say: Lead type in wooden trays. The B is worn nearly flat.
repeat: The exclamation marks have a compartment of their own, and it is the largest.
Every letter is cast backward so that it prints forward. It is the most honest thing in the building and it does it in reverse.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing. It is lead and it has nothing to add.
repeat: A faint rattle of lead when the press starts. The type knows what is coming.
Nothing. Several thousand words in that case, and not one of them in order.

overrides.PICK_UP: The letter B, I notice, is nearly worn out. My name has been spending it.

LOOK_AT.say: Twelve years of the Clarion. The Mott story runs on the front page of one issue in three, and has for twelve years, with nothing new in it.
repeat: Each Mott story gives a different date for the strike. The latest has moved it to a Sunday, for color.
The oldest are yellow and the newest are white, and the story inside them has not aged at all.

LISTEN_TO.say: Paper. Rather a lot of it.
repeat: The stack creaks. Twelve years of news, settling under its own weight.
Nothing. Yesterday's paper has nothing to add to yesterday.

overrides.PULL: The stack is structural. Frame's filing system is masonry.

LOOK_AT.say: The front window, lettered THE CLARION in gold, backward from in here, which is how Frame sees most things.
repeat: People stop outside to read the headline board, then glance in to see whether Frame has noticed them reading. He always has.
The glass is the cleanest thing in the office. He likes to see who is coming before they can deny it.

LISTEN_TO.say: Main Street, and over it someone reading a headline aloud to someone who cannot read. Both of them are pleased.
repeat: The bell over the door, waiting. It rings for news and for creditors and cannot tell them apart.
Boots on the boardwalk, slowing at the glass. Everybody slows here. It is the only place in town the news is free.

LOOK_AT.say: A flatbed press of considerable age, operated by a man of considerable enthusiasm.
repeat: A sheet is half-printed in the bed: CONSOLATION REJOICES. The headline has not yet decided at what.
It is older than the town. It came over the mountains in pieces, which is more effort than anyone has put into the news since.

LISTEN_TO.say: It knocks on the return stroke.
repeat: The knock again, on the return. I could find it in a minute, and he would print that I had broken it.
A long iron sigh as the bed comes home, and then the knock, with the timing of a man repeating a joke.
then: It has been knocking for years and it will not be attended to.

overrides.USE: Frame offered to let me. Then he described the last man's sleeve. I withdrew the request and he printed that I had.
overrides.TALK_TO: It has told more of this town's story than anyone alive, most of it invented. I keep my remarks neutral.

PICK_UP.say: He would print it. He would print it on the front page, and he would spell it GRUBBE.

PUSH.say: He is already leaning toward the next sentence. He does not need help.

USE.say: Everybody in town uses him. He calls it circulation.

GIVE.say: Anything I hand him becomes a story. I am being careful what I hand him.

lamps.note: The lamp hung over the press. A slow, low breath (invariant 9).
The oil lamp on Frame's desk, on its own phase.
